title: Population-Evolve: a Parallel Sampling and Evolutionary Method for LLM Math Reasoning

mechanism.domainTask: Training-free test-time scaling for natural-language mathematical reasoning
mechanism.populationDetail: A fixed-size pool of P solutions is maintained for each question, with no island or tree organization.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive or best-so-far retention is described during evolution.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Every generation contains P independently generated solutions; after a generation is formed, it replaces the prior pool without fitness-based survivor filtering.
mechanism.generationDetail: Each next-generation answer is newly generated from the question and evolving prompt, with the entire prior population as context rather than by editing selected parents.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Correctness verification is used for scoring, but verifier labels or diagnostics are not described as feedback supplied to the evolving prompt; the prompt receives prior answer texts.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No discrete parent selection is performed. Every new candidate receives the complete previous generation as context, but no individual solution is selected as an editable or genealogical parent.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Population-Evolve a Parallel Sampling and Evolutionary Method for LLM Math Reasoning.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Existing from-scratch and generational-replacement placements are supported. The survey's single-model paragraph describes stage-aware temperature variation and cites this paper, but the paper reports fixed temperature 0.6 across trials and no generation-vs-repair temperature schedule. The previous population is prompt context, not selected parents.
